topicName: CI/CD Pipelines for Microservices & Progressive Delivery
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"CI/CD Pipelines for Microservices & Progressive Delivery"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Microservices architectures introduce complexity regarding deployment frequency and release risk. This tutorial explores building robust Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines coupled with progressive delivery strategies like canary releases and feature flags to ensure zero-downtime updates."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of containerization (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Familiarity with CI/CD concepts and pipeline tools (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Argo CD)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Access to a running Kubernetes cluster with a service mesh (e.g., Istio) installed."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Containerizing the Microservice"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Every microservice must be packaged into an immutable container image. Below is a production-ready Dockerfile optimized for a Node.js microservice."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"FROM node:18-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Designing the CI Pipeline"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Continuous Integration pipeline validates code quality, executes unit and integration tests, and builds/pushes the Docker image to a secure registry. Here is a GitHub Actions workflow example:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"name: CI Pipeline
on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]
jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run Tests
        run: npm test
      - name: Log in to Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build and Push Docker Image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v4
        with:
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/myorg/my-microservice:${{ github.sha }}"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Implementing Progressive Delivery with Argo Rollouts"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional Kubernetes Deployments replace old pods with new ones all at once. Progressive delivery uses progressive shifting of traffic to minimize blast radius. We use Argo Rollouts with a Canary strategy."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: my-microservice-rollout
spec:
  replicas: 5
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 20
      - pause: {duration: 10m}
      - setWeight: 50
      - pause: {duration: 10m}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-microservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-microservice
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: server
        image: ghcr.io/myorg/my-microservice:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Automated Rollback via Metrics"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"To achieve true progressive delivery, the pipeline must analyze metrics during the pause phase. If error rates spike, the rollout automatically aborts and rolls back to the stable version."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: success-rate
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: success-rate
    interval: 1m
    successCondition: result[0] >= 0.99
    failureLimit: 3
    provider:
      prometheus:
        address: http://prometheus-service.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9090
        query: |
          sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"2.*",service="my-microservice"}[2m]))
          /
          sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="my-microservice"}[2m]))"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining containerized microservices, automated CI checks, and progressive delivery via Argo Rollouts and Prometheus metrics, engineering teams can release updates continuously and safely without impacting production uptime."}]
